sourceEvidence.label: S0.3 lifecycle reports and privileged companion source at 07a7be2

assessment.summary: The evidence supports centralizing caller identity, replay resistance, monotonic lease state, and final action launch inside the privileged service boundary.

nonNegotiables: Keep the S0.3 owner Binder, per-user stopped check, crash grace, and deterministic exit protections.
Limit all actions to the fixed test source, fixed test target, and non-persistent Back action.
Fail closed when caller identity, signing identity, package state, session state, or lease state is unknown.
Do not add network, root-only, Device Owner, or L3-L5 capabilities.
assumptions: Shizuku v13 supplies the documented Context constructor to the UserService on the target device.
No release-grade memory budget was supplied.
The existing 250 ms Back P95 threshold remains the performance decision boundary.

opportunities.title: Centralize privileged session identity, capability, and final action authorization
opportunities.summary: Make the shell UserService derive caller identity, consume one-time capabilities, own monotonic leases, and serialize final authorization with process launch.
opportunities.diagnosis: S0.3 fixed the observed force-stop failure, but identity, replay, lease, and final action controls remain split between caller conventions, the state machine, and the action launcher.

evidence.claim: The v2 force-stop scenario dispatched one Back after the ordinary app package had been stopped.
The owner-bound v3 protocol revoked with owner_package_stopped, stopped the companion, and dispatched zero Back actions after force-stop.
The startMonitor interface accepts ownerUid as caller-provided data.
The client supplies Process.myUid and a correlation session ID but no separate unlogged one-time capability.
The policy tracks owner attachment and crash grace but has no consumed-session set or independent monotonic session lease.
dispatchBack returns from actionDenialReason before starting the input process.
The privileged authorization invariant is maintained by several cooperating call sites instead of one service-owned boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every owner UID is derived from Binder calling identity and cannot be changed by request fields.
The owner UID maps to the fixed owner package and a resolvable current signing certificate.
Each session ID and 256-bit capability is consumed at most once per UserService process.
Every authorization has an immutable rule snapshot and a server-generated monotonic lease deadline.
Unknown identity, signing, package, lease, replay, revocation, or session state denies the action.
The final stopped-state check, authorization decision, and input process start share one in-process serialization boundary.
Raw capabilities never enter logs or public evidence.

options.title: Strengthen local v3 guards
options.summary: Retain caller-supplied UID and current call structure while adding validation, replay checks, and regression coverage.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It preserves the v3 stopped-state protection but does not create a single authorization owner.
All v3 lifecycle controls remain necessary.
Validation narrows malformed UID use while retaining a caller-declared identity field.
Session replay can be cached, but correlation and authorization remain coupled.
Local state additions handle known cases but control ownership remains dispersed.
Reducing code distance narrows but does not structurally own the check/start transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional guards reject obvious invalid and replayed requests, but caller-declared identity and distributed enforcement remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add malformed UID, repeated session, and lifecycle regressions, then inspect every startMonitor caller.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process or mandatory package-manager hop is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare the existing 100-action P50/P95 metrics with the candidate.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded replay identifiers and small state fields are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm replay history has a fixed maximum and inspect process RSS during the 100-action run.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing process and package-state behavior remains, so compatibility is high but control drift can recur.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rerun all S0.3 scenarios and repeated session-start cycles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a few rejection events are added; no new component requires monitoring.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify each rejection reason is visible without logging raw secrets.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current AIDL and automation shape can remain compatible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing scripts without argument changes and verify old UserService cleanup.

residualRisks: Caller-declared identity remains part of the trusted request.
Future action call sites can drift from the final-check convention.
Replay protection ends with the UserService process.

workPackages: Add local UID/package validation and bounded replay history.
Reduce the check-to-start code gap and add regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed and repeated requests are rejected.
migrationNotes: Retains the weaker caller-declared identity contract.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused guard and test changes to v3.

options.title: Server-derived identity and one-time capability
options.summary: Derive identity at the Binder boundary, consume a separate capability once, enforce a monotonic lease, and serialize final authorization with process start.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It preserves and structurally extends the v3 force-stop protections at the privileged boundary.
The proven owner Binder, stopped check, grace, and exit behavior remains mandatory during migration.
The caller UID field is removed and replaced with Binder-derived identity.
A separate client-internal capability is consumed once and only its fingerprint is observed.
Replay history and a server-generated monotonic lease become policy-owned state.
The policy owns a serialized final-check-and-start operation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Request fields cannot select owner identity, replay and lease state are explicit, and the local check/start gap is closed at one service-owned linearization point.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test mismatched identity, missing signature, repeated session/capability, lease expiry, revocation races, and the S0.3 force-stop scenario.

tradeoffs.assessment: Session start adds PackageManager and certificate digest work; the action path moves the existing stopped query under a lock but adds no extra process spawn.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure session-start latency and compare 100-action detection/Back/leave P50/P95 against v3, with Back P95 limited to 250 ms.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded replay set, owner certificate digests, and immutable snapshot are retained per service process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Cap replay entries, inspect retained object counts, and compare RSS before and after the 100-action run.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unknown identity and package state fail closed with explicit reasons, but Context or PackageManager incompatibility rejects the entire session.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a single identity probe first, then the full lifecycle matrix; record all fail-safe reasons.

tradeoffs.assessment: Events gain caller-identity source, signing digest, capability fingerprint, rule snapshot, and lease metadata without raw capability disclosure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate event fields and scan raw/public evidence for the capability value.

tradeoffs.assessment: AIDL and UserService version change together, requiring a coordinated APK replacement and v3 process cleanup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Install over v3, confirm official destroy runs, and execute existing scripts with unchanged external intent arguments.

residualRisks: Android package stopped changes and input injection cannot be one system-server transaction.
Replay history is process-local and resets when UserService restarts.
The exported command Intent remains a test harness rather than a consumer authorization boundary.
PackageManager behavior in other OEM, multi-user, work-profile, and clone environments remains unverified.

affectedComponents: new owner identity and rule snapshot types
workPackages: Upgrade AIDL and generate client-internal 256-bit capabilities.
Derive and verify owner UID, package, user, and signing identity in UserService.
Implement bounded replay state, immutable rule snapshots, and monotonic leases.
Serialize final stopped-state validation and ProcessBuilder.start.
Run unit, build, lint, lifecycle, race, and performance validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Ready evidence proves Binder-derived UID and non-empty owner signing identity.
Repeated session or capability and expired leases are rejected.
Revocation visible before the linearization point launches zero actions.
S0.2 remains SHIZUKU_POC_FEASIBLE with Back P95 at or below 250 ms.
migrationNotes: Bump UserService version so old v3 code is destroyed.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert to the v3 AIDL, UserService version, policy, and reports; never bypass failed identity checks at runtime.

options.title: Independent signed policy broker
options.summary: Use a normal-UID broker and Android Keystore to sign user-approved, one-time, expiring rule capabilities for UserService verification.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Signed expiry and revocation complement but do not replace the v3 force-stop tactical checks.
Lifecycle controls remain required under the signed capability.
Binder identity and signed issuer identity replace caller-declared UID.
The authorization object becomes signed, one-time, and separable from correlation.
Persistent counters or revocation state can reject replay across UserService restarts.
UserService still owns the final serialized action gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: A dedicated issuer can centralize user-approved rule creation and support cross-process replay resistance, provided every signing path enforces the same user policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model every issuer entry, test key misuse and replay across restarts, and verify UserService accepts only the pinned public key and Binder owner.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authorization creation adds broker IPC and a Keystore signature; action verification adds signature work but can remain outside the polling loop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark grant creation, signature verification, and end-to-end action latency against Option 2.

tradeoffs.assessment: A broker process plus persistent replay and key metadata requires more resident and stored state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure broker and UserService RSS, stored metadata size, and growth under repeated grants.

tradeoffs.assessment: Key invalidation, broker death, restore, and rotation introduce failure modes that must fail closed without permanently locking out the user.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject broker death, key invalidation, app restore, upgrade, and rollback while checking deterministic recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project must observe issuer health, key version, verification failures, revocation state, and rotation progress.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define telemetry and an incident runbook before enabling the broker outside tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: A signed capability schema, key lifecycle, dual verifier window, and persistent replay migration are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype versioned capabilities and prove upgrade plus rollback while old capabilities drain.

residualRisks: A signing broker that lacks a real user-policy gate can cryptographically authorize the same unsafe requests.
Key invalidation and restore can create availability failures.
The final Android system race after local authorization remains.
Complexity can move control drift into signing and rotation paths.

workPackages: Define the user-approved rule creation boundary.
Design and version a signed capability schema and key lifecycle.
Add broker IPC, UserService verification, persistent replay, and rotation.
Validate restore, invalidation, upgrade, rollback, and incident observability.
acceptanceCriteria: Only user-approved broker paths can sign capabilities.
Replay is rejected across UserService restarts.
Key rotation and rollback preserve fail-safe behavior.
migrationNotes: Defer until real dynamic rule and multi-entry authorization requirements exist.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain old verification keys until all issued capabilities expire, disable new issuance, then roll back the broker and schema.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the server-derived capability boundary for the fixed-package S0.4 PoC; reconsider the signed broker when real rule creation, multiple entry points, or cross-process replay resistance becomes a requirement.

openQuestions: Does Binder.getCallingUid in the target Shizuku UserService return the ordinary app UID on every supported backend?
Does the Shizuku v13 Context reliably support package and signing identity lookups across target OEMs and profiles?
Should production authorization reject replay across UserService restarts using a signed broker or persistent counter?
Which published residual-race threshold is acceptable when Android cannot atomically combine package stopped state and input injection?
How will the exported test command Intent be removed or protected before real product integration?
